full_judgment:
This Rule calls in question a judgment and decree of the learned Munsif, First Court, Patuakhali passed in Title Suit No. 56 of 1969. It raise a short but important question as to the scope of section 9 of the Specific Relief Act. 

 2. One Gopal Chandra Dey, predecessor of the opposite parties sued the petitioners for a decree under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act alleging that he was in possession of the disputed land but the defendants forcibly dispossessed him therefrom in the last part of Kartick, 1375 B.S. and erected thatched huts thereon. 

 4. After the trial the learned Munsif who heard the suit found that the plaintiff was in possession of the land in suit, that the defendant had dispossessed him therefrom and that the suit was brought within six months from the date of dispossession. Accordingly he decreed the suit on contest with costs directing recovery of possession of the suit lane by evicting the defendants and demolishing the structures raised by the defendants. Being aggrieved the defendants have challenged the propriety of that order in this Rule. It is contended on behalf of the petitioners that the learned Munsif, has acted beyond his jurisdiction in passing a decree for demolition of the structures raised by the defendants. Consequently the decision suffers from a grave error of law which has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 Nothing in this section shall bar any person from suing to establish his title to such property and to recover possession thereof. No appeal shall lie from any order or decree passed in any suit instituted under this section, nor shall any review of any such order or decree be allowed." 

 6. The above provision clearly lays down that if a person who has without his consent, been dispossessed of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he is entitled to recover possession thereof by filing a suit. A plea of title is no defence in the suit and any decision that may be made in the suit will be subject to a Title Suit which may be eventually filed and the person who has title or even a better right shall be competent to ask for recovery of the property on establishment of such right. As the question of title of the respective parties is kept beyond the purview of such a suit the real intendment behind this provision seems to be to provide a quick remedy by way of restitution of possession only. Under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act. the court has therefore, no power to pass a decree for removal or demolition  of structures. 

 7. The view which I have taken finds support from a decision of the Calcutta High Court in the case of Sana Mia and another Vs. Prokash Chandra Bhattacharjya, A.I.R. 1940 Cal. 464-44 CWN. 895. In that case the propriety of an order under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act directing removal of huts raised by the defendants was challenged as being without jurisdiction. A Single Judge of that Court set aside that part of the decree being of the view that an order is beyond the scope of the section. In course of the judgment Sen, J. observed as follows:-
